name: Lake Kol-Kogur
near: Kok-Oirok — ~12.5 km as the crow flies (OSM); inhabited villages with guesthouses — Kalmak-Ashuu, Karool-Debe, Shabdan, Tar-Suu lower down the Chon-Kemin valley; on the south side of the range — Tamchy on Issyk-Kul (2–3 days' travel over a pass).
elev: About 2470–2500 m: 2468 m (Nomad's Land), 2500 m (Sputnik8, 2026 tour). The value “about 2000 m” (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Silk Road Explore) contradicts other sources and is probably too low.
short: Kol-Kogur is a secluded forest lake on the northern slope of Kungey Ala-Too in Chon-Kemin National Park (~2470 m), formed by an ancient landslide; it can be reached only on foot or on horseback.
desc: Kol-Kogur (Kel-Kogur) lies in the Kemin district in Chon-Kemin State Nature Park on the northern slope of Kungey Ala-Too, at about 2470–2500 m, ~5 km below Kol-Tor Pass. The lake is held by a natural dam from an ancient landslide at its northern end; its waters feed tributaries of the Chon-Kemin (Silk Road Explore). Spruce forests come down to the shore from the west and meadows from the east; the surroundings are home to Turkestan lynx, maral deer and golden eagles. There is no road to the lake: from the Chon-Kemin valley it is a river crossing on horseback and a climb on foot (day tours), or a long approach along the left bank of the Chon-Kemin of 20–25 km; from the Issyk-Kul side — 2–3-day horse routes from Tamchy over passes of ~3320–3342 m.
guide: Kol-Kogur is the “lost lake” of Chon-Kemin: you can't get here by car, and that is its main charm. The fastest way is a day tour: crossing the Chon-Kemin on horses and climbing through spruce forest to the lake at ~2500 m. If you have 3 days, ride from Tamchy over Kol-Tor Pass, starting on the shore of Issyk-Kul and finishing in the Chon-Kemin valley. Pay attention to the northern shore — the lake is dammed by an ancient landslide. Don't try to cross the river on your own: hire horses from locals or CBT.
see: The lake itself with spruce forests on the western shore and meadows on the eastern; the landslide dam at the northern end; the crossing of the Chon-Kemin; views of the Kungey Ala-Too range and Kol-Tor Pass; nearby in the valley — Lake Jashyl-Kol.
skip: You aren't ready for a long day (10–12 h) or a multi-day horse trek — you can't drive up. You're afraid of crossing a turbulent river. You're limited by budget: a one-day jeep tour from Bishkek costs about $420 per group (Sputnik8).
diff: Moderate to hard. One-day option: crossing on horseback + climbing on foot, ~10 h of trail (Sputnik8; “moderate physical effort” in reviews). The walking approach along the left bank is 20–25 km one way, better done over 2 days (hiking.kg). From Tamchy — 3 days on horseback over passes of 3320–3342 m, designed for beginner riders (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, CBT).
when: June to September (CBT Tamchi); for the horse trek from Tamchy — July–August (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). In spring and early summer the Chon-Kemin is in high flow — the crossing is more dangerous.
hours: A natural area of Chon-Kemin National Park, no opening hours. Tours: a one-day trip from Bishkek takes ~12 h; CBT Tamchi — start at 9:00, return on day 3 around 16:30.
daytime: Set off as early in the morning as possible: the one-day route takes ~10 h, and it is safer to cross the river before the daytime rise in water from snowmelt (editorial).
how: From Bishkek along the Balykchy highway through the Boom Gorge, turn into the Chon-Kemin valley in the Kemin district (140 km, 2.5–3 h — ilovekg; to Jashyl-Kol 170 km, 3.5 h — hiking.kg). Then: cross the Chon-Kemin on horses and climb on foot; or approach along the left bank from the bridge downstream (20–25 km, hiking.kg); or from Issyk-Kul from Tamchy over the pass (2–3 days).
needcar: Yes: a car (an SUV on the upper sections of the valley) to the start in Chon-Kemin, plus horses for the crossing/approach. The sources name no regular transport to upper Chon-Kemin.
self: Partly: the walking approach along the left bank of the Chon-Kemin is possible for experienced hikers with a tent and navigation. The river crossing and the horse option — only with locals (CBT, guesthouses). There is no reliable crossing opposite Jashyl-Kol.
roadtype: Paved road to the valley (Bishkek–Balykchy highway); in Chon-Kemin a road that turns to dirt in the upper part (hiking.kg rates the drive to Jashyl-Kol 4 out of 5 for difficulty). To the lake — only a horse/foot trail with a river crossing.
traveltime: Bishkek → Chon-Kemin: 2.5–3 h (140 km, ilovekg); to the upper part of the valley (Jashyl-Kol) — 3.5 h (170 km, hiking.kg). A one-day tour takes 12 h, of which ~10 h is trail. From Tamchy — 2–3 days on horseback.
stay: At the lake — tents only. In the Chon-Kemin valley: CBT Chon-Kemin guesthouse (Karool-Debe, 7 rooms, yurt, 700–1200 som/person — travelbar.kg; +996 771 327 781); Ashuu guesthouse (Kalmak-Ashuu, 2GIS 4.9/5, 168 ratings, ashu.kg, +996 552 700 552); Kordon guest house (Kalmak-Ashuu); Kemin Guest House (Tar-Suu).
net: In the upper part of the Chon-Kemin valley the signal is poor — save offline maps (ilovekg); coverage at the lake is not confirmed (probably none). There is Wi-Fi in the guesthouses lower down (travelbar.kg).
entry: The lake is in Chon-Kemin National Park; tour operators mention the park entrance fee (Trip to Kyrgyzstan: the “park entrance fee” is not included in the tour), but the 2025–2026 amount was not found in open sources. Horses for the crossing are paid separately (Sputnik8).
transfer: One-day jeep tour from Bishkek $420 per group (Sputnik8, 2026); marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek–Balykchy to the turnoff 500–600 som (24.kg, 07.2026). Prices for renting horses and for a taxi to upper Chon-Kemin were not found.
bring: Trekking boots and sandals/spare shoes for the crossing, a rain jacket and warm clothes (2500 m, and storm protection on passes above 3300 m — Trip to Kyrgyzstan), water and food for the whole day, an offline map, a first-aid kit, cash for the horses. For a multi-day trip — a tent and sleeping bag.
warn: Crossing the Chon-Kemin is dangerous, especially during high water (May–July): there is no reliable crossing opposite Jashyl-Kol, and homemade suspension crossings are an unproven method (hiking.kg). There is no signal. It is a national park — follow the rules and don't light fires outside designated camps. Multi-day routes over passes above 3300 m carry a risk of bad weather and altitude sickness.
food: On tours — a picnic by the lake and a Kyrgyz dinner in a mountain cafe (Sputnik8); in Chon-Kemin guesthouses — home-cooked Kyrgyz food (CBT: partial board; CBT Tamchi and Trip to Kyrgyzstan — full board on horse tours). There are no eateries at the lake itself.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 26 ratings (03.10.2026). Sputnik8 (one-day tour, guide Denis): 5.0 — “magical landscapes”, but “moderate physical effort” and cleanliness not perfect in places. No TripAdvisor/2GIS reviews of the lake itself were found.
p.sum: Kol-Kogur (≈2460–2500 m) is the “lost” lake of Chon-Kemin National Park. There is no road to it, and the main obstacle is crossing the Chon-Kemin River. So there are two realistic options. The first is to base yourself at a Chon-Kemin guesthouse (Ashuu in Kalmak-Ashuu, CBT in Karool-Debe, 700–1200 som/person), from where locals will take you across on horses and guide you to the lake in a day (≈10 h). The second is a horse trek from Issyk-Kul from Tamchy over Kol-Tor Pass (3320 m): 32 km and about 5 h in the saddle on the first day, 2–3 days in all. A direct marshrutka (minibus) runs from Bishkek to the Chon-Kemin villages (250 som, Kaktus 02.2026); you can also take a bus toward Balykchy to the turnoff, and then a taxi or a guesthouse transfer. Ready-made jeep tours from Bishkek start at $420 per car; horses for the crossing are paid separately.

p.season: May to early July: high water, the crossing is dangerous. July–August: the best season for the trek from Tamchy. September: stable, less water, cold nights. October–April: guesthouses partly closed, the upper valley and passes under snow
p.budget.economy: ≈4000–7000 som for 2 days: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek–Chon-Kemin 250 som one way, a taxi into the valley (by arrangement), a guesthouse 700–1200 som/person, horses for the crossing and a guide — check with CBT
p.budget.comfort: A day jeep tour $420 per car + horses; a 2-day horse tour $600; a 3-day trek from Tamchy (Nomad's Land, CBT) — on request
p.permits: The sources do not require a border-zone permit for Kol-Kogur (in the “Already known” section only the upper reaches of the Chon-Kemin are marked as a border zone — check for routes to the very upper reaches). The lake is in Chon-Kemin National Park, a fee is charged (weproject 06.2026), but the 2025–26 amount is not published; on Nomad's Land and too.kg tours it is included
p.access: Not for small children, older people or strollers: the crossing and climb take ~10 h. The horse trek from Tamchy is designed for beginner riders, but it is 5 h in the saddle and a pass of 3320 m. The Chon-Kemin valley with its guesthouses suits everyone
